text:
Sam Bennett is still the player who drives opponents mad. On Nov. 12, with Florida down 4-1 in Detroit, Alex DeBrincat dropped the gloves with him, and the Panthers came back to win 5-4. The Hockey News wrote about Red Wings fans wanting DeBrincat as captain afterward. That's the Bennett effect: two Cups, a Conn Smythe in 2025, and a lot of people who'd like to hit him.

His scoring is slower than a year ago: 7 goals and 12 points in 23 games, with his ice time down about a minute and a half over the last ten. The goals are fine (7 on 6.2 expected, including two against Columbus on Nov. 10). The assists aren't, and our numbers flag why: Florida has scored 5.2 fewer goals than its chances with him on the ice. That usually swings back, and it should bring his points with it.

The process is decent. Florida gets about 53% of the expected goals in his minutes, nearly three points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey's warning from last season was penalties and chances against. Watch both as the minutes come back.
